edges.rationale: Mauchly co-designed ENIAC and EDVAC, machines standardly treated as founding events for the practice of building electronic computer systems, and is named directly in the source grounding the existing reviewed von Neumann edge to this same subfield. I did not propose founded_or_formalized: the corpus's own calibration already treats von Neumann -- the person whose report specifically named and described the architecture concept most central to 'computer systems' as a subfield -- as merely 'influenced' at this grain, not a founder, and subfield:computer-systems (ACM CCS 'computer systems organization') spans decades of subsequent research well beyond any one 1940s machine. Giving Mauchly a stronger relation than von Neumann for the identical target would be an inconsistent, inflated claim, so I matched the existing edge's relation instead.
edges.uncertainty: This is a genuine judgment call, not a settled one: the corpus has repeatedly held broad field-grain influence edges for being diffuse (e.g. Cuvier->archaeology, Pearson->sociology, Vernadsky->environmental-science, all currently held per foundry/held.json), and QC may reasonably conclude the same applies here and hold or decline this edge rather than promote it -- a no-edge outcome is legitimate and I do not think it is clearly wrong. Unlike those held cases, Mauchly's link is a direct co-design credit within the very same historical episode the reviewed von Neumann edge already cites, not an indirect diffusion of ideas into an unrelated field, which is why I proposed the edge rather than omitting it outright. I have not live-verified the 'Von Neumann architecture' article's exact current wording this session. The ENIAC patent was later invalidated (Honeywell v. Sperry Rand, 1973) on grounds that some central ideas derived from John Atanasoff's earlier work -- a priority complication this edge's confidence does not attempt to resolve.
